races.name: Thomas Armstrong Group Haydock Park Training Series Apprentice Handicap Stakes (Apprentice Training Race - Part Of The Racing Excellence Series)

runners_data.name: Dream Harder
runners_data.note: A hold-up performer for Mark Loughnane who has shown a preference for 12-14f trips on good ground; recent form figures of 6-6-8 suggest a horse out of form, and nothing in the profile screams soft-ground 1m6f winner today.

runners_data.name: Yellow Card
runners_data.note: Mickey Bowen's four-year-old has a striking CV at 20-22f trips on good ground, and the step back to 1m6f on soft is a significant query — sim-going record of 0 wins and 0 places from three attempts underlines the concern, with 56 days off adding uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Gentle Warrior
runners_data.note: K.R. Burke's four-year-old carries visored headgear and ran with promise when second at 14f on good, but the horse's natural running style means it will not be racing where it wants to today — its 1W3P sim-going record shows ability to hit the frame in testing conditions, but the position it ends up in will not reflect its instincts.

runners_data.name: Dance Time
runners_data.note: David Loughnane's six-year-old is the most consistent horse in the field, running to a placed figure in recent starts including second at 14f on good; travelling prominently is its natural mode and this race shape, with a lone front-runner and no pressure, gives it a clear tactical opportunity over a trip it has handled.

runners_data.name: Expressionless
runners_data.note: Dylan Cunha's six-year-old has a record that includes a win and placed runs in similar going conditions, and p-headgear is noted; a genuine hold-up horse that will be trying to do its racing in a position further forward than comfortable, and Kyle McHugh will need to manage that tension over 1m6f.

runners_data.name: Zimmerman
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's seven-year-old arrives on the back of a win at 16f on soft just three days ago — the quick turnaround is unusual and worth monitoring — and the sim-going and trip profile are a genuine match; tp-headgear, and the horse's true hold-up instincts mean it will need Cascade Hall to empty in the straight.

runners_data.name: Cascade Hall
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's seven-year-old is the only confirmed front-runner in the field, shown to handle soft ground (placed at 16f on soft), and with h-headgear fitted; uncontested in front over a staying trip on testing ground, Shay Farmer simply needs to conserve energy through the early stages and Cascade Hall becomes very hard to pass.

runners_data.name: Easwrith Destiny
runners_data.note: David Menuisier's three-year-old is the least exposed horse in the field with only four runs, and importantly has form at 10f on soft ground (placed); the step up to 1m6f is a significant question mark but prominent racing style gives tactical access to the pace, and youth could mean improvement is possible.

races.paceDynamic: Cascade Hall is the sole confirmed front-runner in this eight-runner field and, with no rival likely to seriously contest the lead, will stride out alone on soft ground over 1m6f at Haydock and set a tempo entirely of their own choosing. Dance Time and Easwrith Destiny are the only other prominent-style runners, meaning Cascade Hall faces minimal early pressure and can dictate every yard at a comfortable, energy-conserving clip. On soft ground over an extended trip with a lone pace-setter controlling fractions, hold-up horses will need a strong finishing burst that this controlled tempo may not generate — placing a premium on the runners closest to the action rather than those deepest in the field. This shape heavily favours prominent and stalking profiles who can travel within range of Cascade Hall without expending energy, and pounce when the pace inevitably flattens out in testing ground. The field contains more genuine hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear — Gentle Warrior, Expressionless, and Zimmerman are all natural hold-up horses redistributed to midfield positions they are unlikely to naturally secure given the limited number ahead of them.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Cascade Hall Dictates Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Cascade Hall sets a soft, uncontested lead and controls the tempo from flag to finish on yielding ground.
scenarios.body: Cascade Hall gets away cleanly and the soft ground rewards a horse that has been placed in staying trips before, dictating a pace no rival can wind up from behind; Dance Time or Easwrith Destiny, close enough in prominent spots, are best positioned to challenge in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If Dance Time or Easwrith Destiny tracks Cascade Hall closely and produces a superior finish in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: The moderate early tempo set by Cascade Hall suits a horse that can settle within a length or two and produce a sustained run on soft ground; Dance Time's consistent placed form at 14f and Easwrith Destiny's soft-ground experience make both live dangers to the front-runner.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Closer Gets Home
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the straight and redistributed hold-up horses, particularly Zimmerman, find enough daylight to finish strongly.
scenarios.body: Zimmerman arrives with a recent win over this exact 16f trip on soft ground, and if the race develops into a true slog the horses with the freshest legs furthest back could benefit; however, the comfortable tempo makes a winning late run against a fresh Cascade Hall unlikely, and Zimmerman's natural hold-up style will mean covering extra ground.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Field Bunches, Chaos Ensues
scenarios.trigger: If the field compresses into a tight bunch on the turn for home and jockey errors or interference disrupt the race shape.
scenarios.body: In an apprentice race over an extended trip on soft ground, inexperienced riders may misjudge positions and create crowding, giving an outsider a fortunate route through; Yellow Card, with a winning mark over 20-22f on good ground, remains an unknown quantity on this shorter trip in soft conditions but could benefit from a messy race.

watchPoints.text: Cascade Hall — if Shay Farmer gets away cleanly and there is no rival within three lengths by the first bend, the lone front-runner has a clear path to dominate on soft ground with zero pressure applied.

Zimmerman — running just three days after its last start is unusual at this level; monitor in the paddock and early in the race for any signs of fatigue, as a quick turnaround on soft ground over 1m6f is a significant physical ask.

Yellow Card — Isobelle Chalmers' three-pound claim may tempt punters but the trip is shorter than this horse's preferred range of 20-22f and the sim-going record shows no wins or places in comparable conditions, making it a significant profile mismatch.

Dance Time — the only prominent-style runner with consistent placed form over similar trips; watch whether Conor Whiteley positions close enough to Cascade Hall in the first half-mile, as the entire race outcome for this horse depends on that early tactical decision.

Easwrith Destiny — Donagh Murphy partners a lightly-raced three-year-old stepping up markedly in trip; watch for signs of greenness or waywardness in the straight, which could compromise what is otherwise a well-placed prominent runner.

races.name: Lee Thomas Christy Memorial Ebf Fillies' Novice Stakes (gbb Race)
Tattersalls £40,000 Ebf Fillies' Novice Stakes (gbb Race)

runners_data.name: Etonnante
runners_data.note: K.R. Burke's filly has placed figures of 7-1 over 6f at Goodwood and arrives 56 days since her last run; she is the lone pace-setter here and her STYLE_FIT tag reflects that she typically races prominently rather than truly leading, so how fluently she settles in front on soft ground is the key variable.

runners_data.name: Californian Angel
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's filly carries an OR of 120 off form figures of 6-3 at Goodwood; she is a genuine hold-up type whose mapping to midfield is a consequence of the field's makeup rather than her natural race pattern — she will likely sit furthest back and needs the others to come back to her.

runners_data.name: Marsala
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's filly has recent experience on Tapeta at Wolverhampton (7f) and Goodwood soft form figures of 4, suggesting she stays well; placed 23 days ago, she is the freshest of the closers and Beckett's runners often improve markedly second time out on a true soft surface.

runners_data.name: Novah
runners_data.note: Nigel Tinkler's filly posted a bare 8 on debut at Goodwood 21 days ago and carries a fade-in-finish flag; Tinkler's 0/21 fourteen-day stat offers no encouraging stable momentum, and her profile is the least compelling of the hold-up quartet unless debut greenness masked significant ability.

races.paceDynamic: Etonnante is the sole confirmed front-runner in this four-runner field and, with no rival likely to challenge her for the lead, she will stride out from the gates on soft ground at Haydock and set a controlled, sustainable gallop over 6f. The three hold-up fillies — Californian Angel, Marsala, and Novah — will be forced to track or sit behind, creating a clean, processional shape with Etonnante dictating every yard. On soft ground a single, uncontested pace-setter who can control tempo is unlikely to tie herself up early, which means the race may develop into a test of which closers can generate sufficient momentum off a steady fractions. This shape strongly favours a strong-finishing hold-up type capable of producing one sustained late run, provided Etonnante does not steal it with a well-judged front-running display; genuine prominent-racing types who can sit just off the pace and quicken on soft ground are the primary beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Etonnante Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Etonnante bowls clear from the gates and settles into a rhythm that the hold-up trio cannot bridge in the final 2f.
scenarios.body: Etonnante sets an uncontested pace on soft ground, conserving energy through the early stages before kicking again from 2f out; with no rival applying pressure she never has to burn her reserves and the hold-up horses, starting their runs from well back, simply run out of ground.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Swamp Late
scenarios.trigger: If Etonnante goes slightly quicker than the soft ground rewards and ties up inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: The hold-up trio close rapidly as Etonnante's stride shortens under soft-ground fatigue, and the filly with the strongest finish off a sound staying pedigree gets up close home; this suits Californian Angel or Marsala, both capable of a strong late surge.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Marsala Sweeps Through
scenarios.trigger: If Marsala's extra stamina (7f form on Tapeta) translates well to soft 6f and she produces the strongest single run of the four.
scenarios.body: Marsala sits last early, absorbs the steady gallop, and picks up widest of all in the straight; the soft ground extending the race's relative test of stamina plays to her profile against less experienced fillies.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Novah Recovers Form
scenarios.trigger: If Novah's poor debut form figure is entirely explained by greenness and she strips sharper at this second start.
scenarios.body: Novah's ⚠ fade flag and bare form figure of 8 make this the least likely outcome, but if she has learned from her debut she could track Etonnante throughout and outstay her in the closing stages on soft ground.

watchPoints.text: Etonnante — watch whether Clifford Lee settles her cleanly in front; if she over-races or is allowed to set a punishing fractions on soft ground she will be vulnerable to all three closers in the final furlong.

Californian Angel — her true running style places her at the back of just four runners, meaning she will need soft-ground stamina to close a gap created by a controlled, energy-saving front-runner; any lack of pace injection from the leaders works directly against her.

Marsala — her Tapeta form over 7f suggests she may be the most effective stayer in the field, but her Goodwood 6f figure of 4 on Good ground leaves a question over whether she can quicken sharply enough on soft going when the race is run at a steady tempo.

Novah — Faye McManoman takes over in the saddle here; watch whether the booking reflects a stable confidence signal or is simply a logistical choice, as Tinkler's 0/21 recent trainer strike rate suggests caution.

Soft going confirmed for all races on the card — the ground has not deteriorated beyond Soft, which slightly favours a front-runner who can control fractions rather than a deep, stamina-sapping surface that would more decisively assist the hold-up horses.

races.name: Oakmere Homes Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Milford
runners_data.note: Wears a visor and has shown ability on better ground at Goodwood, but soft Haydock 6f is a slightly different test; hold-up style suits a strong pace but Tom Kiely-Marshall's 5lb claim adds appeal if the filly can get a clear run from the back.

runners_data.name: Wild Clary
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner and sole pace-setter in this field, Clifford Lee should be able to lead unchallenged; won on soft at 6f previously and holds strong claims if the controlled tempo she sets favours her own galloping style over the entire trip.

runners_data.name: Territorial Knight
runners_data.note: Tom Eaves's mount has placed on soft ground at 6f and will look to race prominently; Kevin Ryan's yard is in form (T14: 4/37) and a handy position from the outset suits this horse's profile in what looks a well-organised tactical setup.

runners_data.name: Kodi Lion
runners_data.note: Prominent racer whose recent form has been poor across soft and good ground at 6f and 7f, with five finishes of 9th or worse in the last five runs; Cieren Fallon's booking provides some reassurance but the overall profile here is concerning.

runners_data.name: Woven
runners_data.note: A 10-year-old veteran with nine soft-ground runs in the sample and proven ability at 6f on this type of surface; Connor Beasley rides and Dods has him fit after 60 days off, though age means winning form is increasingly hard to recapture.

runners_data.name: Reciprocated
runners_data.note: Three-year-old carrying 135lbs who has struggled in recent outings, including 11th on soft and 15th on good; Laura Pearson rides and the horse does have a soft-ground win to its name but current form figures of 3-0-0-0 are uninspiring.

runners_data.name: Never Just A Dream
runners_data.note: Callum Rodriguez partners this 6-year-old who has limited soft-ground form (one run, unplaced) and a poor recent record; hold-up style is unlikely to be rewarded unless the pace genuinely hotts up, which looks improbable here.

runners_data.name: Coachello
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old hold-up type with consistent placed efforts in stable conditions but recent runs on soft have yielded an 8th and 11th; Jack Mitchell takes the ride and the visor is applied, though age and going combine to limit expectations.

runners_data.name: Cargin Bhui
runners_data.note: Won twice on standard-to-slow at 6f and arrives after 145 days off, which is a notable freshness flag; Oisin Orr rides for Barron, and while the form figures look solid, this horse's natural rear-of-the-field style means it won't get its ideal position in a field stacked with hold-up types.

runners_data.name: Grant Wood
runners_data.note: David Nolan partners this 7-year-old whose recent form string is entirely on good ground at Goodwood with nothing better than 4th; a genuine hold-up horse whose soft-ground sample is thin (2 runs), and the crowded rear means it will need to race closer than it prefers.

runners_data.name: Ran Amok
runners_data.note: David Probert returns on a horse that has been genuinely competitive on soft, including a second at 6f and multiple placed efforts; Hugo Palmer's runner (T14: 3/30) carries a hood and has the best soft-ground profile of the prominent racers — 76 days off is the only minor concern.

runners_data.name: Lord Bertie
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's 6-year-old carries a flag for fading in the finish, and six starts on soft produced a win and three places but also a 10th and 12th in more recent efforts; a true hold-up horse who, when forced forward by the field's overcrowded rear, is unlikely to produce his best.

runners_data.name: Tip Foster
runners_data.note: Lightly raced 3-year-old with just two runs, including a win at 7f and a third at 6f on soft — that placed effort on this type of going is the most relevant piece of evidence; Joanna Mason rides and 91 days off could mean she arrives fresh, but the experience gap in a 14-runner handicap is significant.

runners_data.name: Trust Amy
runners_data.note: Three-year-old for Gary Hanmer with a third on soft in her recent history and decent placed efforts, but the field's hold-up congestion means Gina Mangan will be unable to position her naturally at the rear; the true running style being compromised in this shape reduces her chance considerably.

races.paceDynamic: Wild Clary is the one confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine pace rival likely to challenge from the front, she should be able to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop on soft ground over 6f at Haydock. Territorial Knight, Kodi Lion, Reciprocated, and Ran Amok will push to race prominently behind her, giving the race a compressed early shape rather than a burning pace — on soft ground, that controlled tempo risks producing a muddling gallop that suits those close to the action rather than those coming from deep. The field holds significantly more hold-up types than the pace map can accommodate at the rear — Grant Wood, Cargin Bhui, Lord Bertie, and Trust Amy are all true back-of-the-field horses who will be forced to race in a more midfield berth than natural, compromising their ability to deliver a late run. The tactical verdict favours prominent racers who can track the controlled pace of Wild Clary and quicken from a handy position on the soft Haydock surface, with genuine hold-up horses disadvantaged both by their compromised positions and by a tempo unlikely to be strong enough to set up a sustained late charge.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Wild Clary Controls; Prominent Prevail
scenarios.trigger: If Wild Clary leads at a soft-ground sustainable tempo and rivals race prominently behind her without disruption.
scenarios.body: Wild Clary dictates from the front at a metronomic pace that rewards those travelling closest, with Territorial Knight, Ran Amok, and Reciprocated positioned to pounce turning for home; soft ground extends the emphasis on travelling well rather than finishing fast, rewarding prominent racers who conserve energy early.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Contested Pace; Closers Capitalise
scenarios.trigger: If Territorial Knight or Reciprocated pushes Wild Clary harder early, lifting the tempo and opening the door for those tracking slightly deeper.
scenarios.body: A stronger early pace on soft ground will cause front-runners to tie up late, allowing horses like Milford or Woven — who can settle off the pace and still travel — to close meaningfully in the final furlong; this scenario requires genuine pressure on Wild Clary that currently looks unlikely given the field's overall hold-up bias.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Soft Ground Stamina Test
scenarios.trigger: If the going deteriorates or the pace is strong enough to turn this into a true stamina examination over the 6f.
scenarios.body: A grinding finish on deepening soft ground will expose horses who lack the staying power or soft-ground pedigree, and will instead favour those with proven ability in these conditions; Ran Amok has shown strong form on soft and Territorial Knight has soft-ground placed efforts, making both well-suited if the race becomes a slog.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Flier Beats Traffic
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to string the field out and leave a clear late run for a true closer.
scenarios.body: This is the least likely shape given that Grant Wood, Cargin Bhui, Lord Bertie, and Trust Amy will all be forced to race closer than their natural style dictates, meaning none will be in the back-of-the-field position needed to produce a winning late burst; even if the scenario partially materialises, their compromised positions make a decisive hold-up winner highly improbable.

watchPoints.text: Wild Clary's ability to control the pace unchallenged is the single biggest factor — if she gets a soft lead, she becomes extremely dangerous and could steal a winning advantage that no hold-up horse can bridge on soft ground.

Territorial Knight and Ran Amok are the most credible threats to Wild Clary if either can secure a prominent position and maintain contact through the bend — watch the draw and early positioning as the stalls open.

The cluster of redistributed hold-up horses — Grant Wood, Cargin Bhui, Lord Bertie, and Trust Amy — will all be forced to race closer than ideal; monitor whether any get trapped in traffic mid-pack, which would effectively end their chances in a race unlikely to produce a strong late pace.
Tip Foster is lightly raced but placed on soft at 6f — watch market moves closer to post time as a fresh, unexposed 3-year-old with proven soft-ground form could be underestimated in the handicap.

Soft ground at Haydock has historically produced compressed fields where prominent racers dominate; if the going worsens further through the card, the advantage for Wild Clary and those tracking her closely increases.

races.name: Aesterius At Bearstone Stud Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Changeofmind
runners_data.note: Won over this exact 5f Soft combination (1/5f/SOF) and has a second similar-going win in the form book; hold-up style is ideally suited when a strong pace is on, and Zak Wheatley's light claiming allowance is a genuine plus at the weights.

runners_data.name: Secret Mistral
runners_data.note: Front-runner who has been in consistent form — placed four times recently — but has only one soft-ground run in the last 15 (unplaced); Tony Carroll's yard is 7/55 over 14 days, which is a moderate strike rate, and sharing the lead duties with two rivals is the key threat to its chance.

runners_data.name: Mighty Magnus
runners_data.note: Three-year-old hold-up horse with solid handicap form over 5f on Good, but all five recent runs have come on that surface; the step up in ground testing to Soft is unproven, and Michael Dods's 3/26 14-day rate offers modest confidence.

runners_data.name: Jer Batt
runners_data.note: Genuine front-runner with five recent placings over 5f on Good but limited soft-ground runs and none producing a win; David & Nicola Barron have 0/10 over 14 days, and Jer Batt must fight for the lead against two rivals from stall one side which could see it use significant energy early.

runners_data.name: Accrual
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with a recent soft-ground placing (3/5f/SOF) and a Goodwood win on Good; Ruth Carr's yard is 0/23 over 14 days which tempers confidence, but the style suits a strong-pace scenario and William Pyle is an economical claimer.

runners_data.name: Lipsink
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with two recent soft-ground placings and a win on Soft over 5f — the going is genuinely in its favour; nine-year-old but clearly still competitive, and a 6-day turnaround for Michael Appleby suggests the horse is in a good place.

runners_data.name: Parisiac
runners_data.note: Holds multiple soft-ground form figures including 2/6f/SOF and 2/5f/SOF plus a win on Good; prominent style suits this pace map well, the cheek-pieces are retained, and Iain Jardine's yard is a solid 3/29 over 14 days.

runners_data.name: Spoof
runners_data.note: Eleven-year-old hold-up horse with the strongest soft-ground record in the field — 3 wins from 11 soft-ground runs — and last won over this exact 5f/Soft combination; the 87-day break is a concern, but Jack Mitchell is an experienced handler and Spoof's profile fits the expected race shape as well as any runner.

runners_data.name: Boston Dan
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's in-form yard (10/87 over 14 days) is the headline angle for this three-year-old, and there is soft-going form worth noting; however, Boston Dan's natural style is hold-up — in this pace-heavy field he is likely to be racing closer to midfield than he would prefer, which the STYLE_FIT tag of 0.93 reflects, tempering expectations accordingly.

runners_data.name: American Bay
runners_data.note: Prominent racer whose recent form string is largely Goodood-ground, with no soft-ground runs in the last five; the OR drop to 72 gives David Nolan a light enough weight but the going question is genuine and Paul Midgley is 3/16 over 14 days.

runners_data.name: Creative Queen
runners_data.note: William Haggas's three-year-old filly has won on Soft (1/6f/SOF) and has blinkers applied; she is a confirmed front-runner who will be ridden positively by Cieren Fallon, and if she can slip the field early she represents a clear danger, though contesting the lead against two rivals makes that scenario uncertain.

runners_data.name: Moonstone Boy
runners_data.note: Jennie Candlish's five-year-old returns from a 147-day break, which is a significant fitness question over sharp 5f on Soft; his natural running style is hold-up, but the congested field means he is likely to find himself in a less rearward position than ideal — the lengthy absence compounds the concern about his ability to finish off his race.

races.paceDynamic: Secret Mistral, Jer Batt, and Creative Queen are all confirmed front-runners in a 12-runner field, meaning at least three horses will be actively competing for the lead from the off over 5f on Soft ground at Haydock — a combination that almost guarantees a strong, searching gallop with no let-up. The pace battle will begin at the gates and the fractions will be quick relative to the ground, burning off horses with limited stamina reserves and punishing any runner who has to work hard in the first two furlongs to secure a position. This race shape historically favours hold-up horses who can conserve energy behind a contested lead and finish with a sustained effort as the pace-setters tie each other up — Changeofmind, Spoof, Accrual, and Mighty Magnus are the profiles who benefit most from this scenario. The field also holds more genuine rear-division types than the map can accommodate at the back — Boston Dan and Moonstone Boy are natural hold-up horses who, in this traffic-heavy pace scenario, are likely to find themselves racing somewhat closer than ideal, diluting their ability to produce a clean late run.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace War, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the three front-runners burn each other off through fast early fractions on soft ground, setting up a truly run race.
scenarios.body: Secret Mistral, Jer Batt, and Creative Queen contest the lead hard from the jump, generating genuine pace that taxes them all before halfway; horses who settled comfortably in behind are able to sustain their finish through the closing stages as the pace-setters fade.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Leader Clears Field
scenarios.trigger: If one front-runner establishes a clear advantage quickly while the others fail to press, allowing a controlled lead.
scenarios.body: Creative Queen, aided by William Haggas's strong 14-day record and Cieren Fallon's tactical awareness, may steal a march if Jer Batt misses the break or Secret Mistral is checked at the start; a horse controlling its own fractions on soft ground can prove difficult to reel in over 5f.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalkers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong but not truly suicidal, allowing prominent-raced horses sitting just off the lead to pounce inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Lipsink and Parisiac, both versatile prominent racers with proven soft-ground form, are ideally positioned to track the contested lead without burning energy and benefit from a slight easing of pace in the final 100 yards.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Beaten For Position
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is surprisingly moderate, allowing front-runners to coast and leaving hold-up horses with too much ground to make up.
scenarios.body: With Boston Dan and Moonstone Boy already racing out of their natural hold-up roles due to field congestion, any softening of early fractions leaves the true rear-division runners with an impossible task; the race would be settled among the front three and prominent types long before the finish line.

watchPoints.text: Secret Mistral, Jer Batt, and Creative Queen all want to lead — watch the first two furlongs for a fierce pace battle that could burn all three out before halfway, opening the race for hold-up horses.

Moonstone Boy returns from 147 days off for Jennie Candlish — watch for signs of race-rustiness in the paddock and early stages; a hold-up horse needing a strong gallop that has missed significant time is vulnerable.

Boston Dan's natural hold-up style is compromised by the volume of pace in this field — watch whether David Allan is forced to chase the pace early, which would effectively race him out of his best position and undermine his finish.

Spoof has the best soft-ground record in the race (3 wins on Soft over this trip) but is 87 days off — watch the betting market for any money that suggests connections are happy with its fitness after the break.

Changeofmind's winning form over 5f Soft with Zak Wheatley's 3lb claim brings it to a potentially well-handicapped mark — watch for any market move that signals Declan Carroll's camp fancies its chances under the pace scenario.

races.name: Arete Foundation Fillies' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Folkene
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with a poor recent run record at 7f on good ground (best sim-going form is 0 wins 0 places from 8 runs), and soft ground adds a further stamina question; Joanna Mason rides but Roger Fell's 14-day strike rate is modest, and a high weight of 139lbs on this ground is a concern.

runners_data.name: Pickersgill
runners_data.note: Ran just two days ago, which is an immediate red flag for fitness and recovery; Paul Mulrennan partners but the horse is predominantly a 6f performer stepping up to 7f in soft ground, and its soft-going record (one top-3 from 15 attempts) is bleak.

runners_data.name: Homestrait
runners_data.note: Genuine prominent racer who has placed at 7f on good ground repeatedly and won over the trip; soft ground is untested (only one sim-going run) but Brian Ellison's stable is operating at a decent clip and Tom Kiely-Marshall's claim could offset the weight; the horse's authentic prominent style puts it in the ideal position when the three front-runners fight.

runners_data.name: Magic Music
runners_data.note: Has a win over 7f on good ground and has placed at this trip before; Steph Hollinshead's yard is in light form but Luke Catton's 3lb claim is useful at 136lbs; soft going is untested from the form string, but the horse's prominent style is authentic and it is well-placed to take advantage of a hot pace.

runners_data.name: Dream Illusion
runners_data.note: Has placed twice at 7f on standard-to-slow surfaces (2nd at Southwell twice), showing some stamina credentials; David Probert is a useful booking, but the horse's hold-up tendency means it depends on a strongly run race and a clean passage to produce its best.

runners_data.name: Clementines Star
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with a 7f win on good and a placed run at 7f on standard; William Carver rides and the Kubler yard has no 14-day wins; the soft ground is the key unknown, but if the horse can avoid being swamped early, its course-distance form is competitive.

runners_data.name: Toralou
runners_data.note: Despite sitting in midfield on the pace map, this is a genuine hold-up horse displaced by an overcrowded back-of-the-field; its best recent effort (2nd) came over 8f on soft, suggesting soft ground is a positive, but Mark Loughnane's 14-day figures are blank and the horse will struggle to replicate a true closing run from a position it did not choose.

runners_data.name: Imelda
runners_data.note: Front-runner with consistent placed form over 7f, including a 2nd at this trip on standard-to-slow; Hector Crouch is a capable rider but a 56-day absence is notable, and if the three-way pace battle wears Imelda down early, it may not last home in soft ground.

runners_data.name: Cypriot Diaspora
runners_data.note: Most recently won over 8f on good, and has placed at that trip in similar conditions; Rod Millman sends this 5-year-old a quick turnaround (7 days) and soft ground is a concern given the horse's form base on quicker surfaces; a confirmed front-runner who adds to pace pressure but may find 7f soft on the sharp side.

runners_data.name: Gelato
runners_data.note: Has a win over 8f on soft and some placed efforts in testing conditions, making the going less of a worry than for others; Finley Marsh is inexperienced at this level and Adrian Wintle's yard is lightly active, but this hold-up type's genuine soft-ground stamina gives it an outside interest in a truly run race.

runners_data.name: Only Dream Big
runners_data.note: Placed once at 7f on good but predominantly a 9f+ performer; a true hold-up horse whose natural style has been pushed forward on the map due to field congestion, meaning it will not get the late-closing run it needs, and Tim Easterby's stable sends it back just 10 days after its last run with a hood noted.

runners_data.name: Light The Night Up
runners_data.note: Has finished 4th or 5th in every recent start, a reliable non-winner profile; K.R. Burke is a strong trainer but the horse has never won, its soft-going record is thin, and as a genuine hold-up type mapped out of position, it faces the same structural disadvantage as the other redistributed closers in this shape.

races.paceDynamic: Imelda, Clementines Star, and Cypriot Diaspora are all confirmed front-runners, guaranteeing a strong, contested gallop from the outset over 7f on soft ground at Haydock — a stamina-sapping combination that will expose any horse lacking genuine resolution. The three leaders will fight for position early, meaning no one controls the pace cleanly, and the fractions will be fast enough to drain those who commit fully through the first half-mile. In soft going over this trip at Haydock, a contested early pace typically sets up a grinding finish that rewards horses with proven stamina, class through the mud, and the ability to travel smoothly just off the speed. The race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can tuck in behind the scrapping leaders and produce a sustained challenge in the final two furlongs, rather than true hold-up horses needing a clean sprint finish. The field holds more genuine hold-up types than the rear of the field can accommodate — Toralou, Only Dream Big, and Light The Night Up have all been redistributed to midfield positions they would not naturally seek, meaning Homestrait and Magic Music are best placed to exploit the contested pace from their authentic prominent berths.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the three front-runners fire from the gate and set a genuinely testing gallop, draining the leaders before the turn.
scenarios.body: Clementines Star, Imelda, and Cypriot Diaspora fight for supremacy and burn each other out through the soft ground, leaving the race to a horse who has travelled smoothly just behind them; Homestrait and Magic Music are ideally profiled to pounce on a tiring lead in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Leader Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If one of the front-runners — most likely Clementines Star or Imelda — establishes a clear lead while the others fail to match strides early.
scenarios.body: A controlled gallop from the front on soft ground suits a front-runner who can dictate their own fractions and has the stamina to see out 7f; Clementines Star's recent win at this trip and Imelda's consistency make them the logical beneficiaries if their rivals fade back.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Soft Ground Stamina Test
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is truly relentless and the soft conditions take a severe toll, turning the race into a battle of attrition in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Horses with the best proven stamina and soft-ground form come into their own as the field strings out; Gelato's win on soft over 8f and Dream Illusion's placed efforts on slow surfaces give them some claim if the race is truly ground out.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses suddenly and hold-up horses get an unexpected route through from off the pace.
scenarios.body: This shape is the least likely given that Toralou, Only Dream Big, and Light The Night Up are all genuine hold-up horses who have been pushed forward out of their natural position and will not find the clean late-running lane they need; even if they do get gaps, their soft-going records are modest and they lack the sprint the scenario demands.

watchPoints.text: Pickersgill ran two days ago — monitor market moves and any reported fitness concerns before the off, as a horse returning this quickly in soft ground is a significant welfare and performance risk.

Imelda has not run for 56 days; watch how Hector Crouch positions her early — if she is slow to stride and loses her front-running spot to Clementines Star or Cypriot Diaspora, her chance evaporates quickly.

Toralou, Only Dream Big, and Light The Night Up are all being mapped to midfield positions they would not naturally seek — if any of them drift wide early trying to find cover, they could cause trouble for authentic midfield horses like Homestrait and Magic Music.

Cypriot Diaspora returns on a 7-day turnaround for Rod Millman; watch whether the horse travels as fluently as its recent win suggested or shows signs of fatigue through the soft ground in the final two furlongs.

The weight burden is significant across the board in soft ground — Folkene (139lbs) and Pickersgill (137lbs) carry the most; if the pace is truly gruelling, top-weighted hold-up horses are at a compounding disadvantage and should be monitored for tiring runs.

races.name: Betfair Supports Racing Welfare Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Hamadhan
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator for Jennie Candlish who has decent soft-ground form (1 win from 7 similar-going runs) but has been well beaten in recent outings, returning after 97 days off; the step up to 1m3½f could help but needs things to fall right from the rear.

runners_data.name: Flash Bardot
runners_data.note: Six-year-old who has a solid record on soft ground (2 places from 15 similar-going runs) and stays well beyond today's trip — Henrietta Knight sends her back after 113 days off, and the testing ground over this distance is squarely in her wheelhouse.

runners_data.name: Lightning Tiger
runners_data.note: Consistent type who keeps hitting the frame (four 4th-place finishes in recent runs) and has soft-ground experience; tongue-tie fitted, trained by Charlie Fellowes, and the 41-day gap looks routine — a danger if the race develops into a grind.

runners_data.name: Yokohama
runners_data.note: In truth a genuine hold-up horse whose natural style means he will be operating closer to midfield than ideal given the field's composition, carrying a 0.93 style-fit flag; John Butler's five-year-old won on good ground and has placed on soft, and Conor Whiteley (5) takes the ride after a 73-day break.

runners_data.name: Tortured Soul
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll's six-year-old has a string of placings on standard ground and is a true hold-up type squeezed into a midfield slot by the sheer volume of closers in this field; his form is exclusively on standard ground which raises soft-ground uncertainty, and Molly Gunn (5) keeps the ride.

runners_data.name: Made All
runners_data.note: Ironically named hold-up horse that Sam England sends out 28 days after its last run; tongue-tie applied, and while it has placed at distances up to 17f on good ground, the soft surface and the fact it will not get its preferred rearmost position (style-fit 0.90) temper its prospects.

runners_data.name: Blue Wonder
runners_data.note: Hughie Morrison's four-year-old won on soft ground (1W1P from 10 similar-going runs) and holds obvious soft-ground claims — the concern is it has been in hold-up mode and will find itself operating closer to midfield than ideal, with a style-fit score of 0.93 flagging the position compromise.

runners_data.name: Star Time
runners_data.note: The race's one confirmed pace-setter; Alan King sends him out 23 days after his last run, and he has the course to himself at the front, with no confirmed rival to pressure him — soft ground is not a proven concern but his recent form figures (82-583) suggest he tends to fade rather than quicken clear.

runners_data.name: Marianita
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's three-year-old is lightly raced (only three career runs) and steps up significantly in distance and field size; Hector Crouch rides and all form has come on standard ground, so both the soft going and the 1m3½f trip represent unknowns.

runners_data.name: Naturalia
runners_data.note: Donald Whillans's five-year-old has won on soft and placed prolifically (1W3P from 15 similar-going runs), making her the most natural pace companion for Star Time and arguably the one with the best credentials to press from a prominent position; form figures of 222441 show consistency and she warrants serious consideration.

runners_data.name: Lesrico
runners_data.note: Lisa Williamson's six-year-old has a strong record on soft ground (1W3P from 13 similar-going runs) and won on soft; headgear note (hh) and Ben Ffrench Davis (5) in the saddle, returning after 25 days — the style-fit flag (0.92) signals he is a true closer who will be nearer midfield than ideal.

runners_data.name: Green Falcon
runners_data.note: David Menuisier's three-year-old has a placed run on soft but has been well beaten on his last two starts including a 13th — a genuine hold-up type mapped into midfield by default, not by preference; trainer has had no winners in 14 days, and stepping up in trip and distance is speculative.

runners_data.name: Ziggy's Avenger
runners_data.note: Michael Bell's three-year-old won on good ground over shorter and has been placed at 8f; today's 1m3½f on soft represents a considerable test of stamina for a horse whose recent form is over trips well short of this, and while mapped mid-pack it is by redistribution rather than natural inclination.

races.paceDynamic: Star Time is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 13-runner field and looks set to bowl along at a sustainable gallop on soft ground, with Naturalia likely to press from a prominent position and ensure at least a workable pace rather than a crawl. With only one genuine pace-setter and a host of horses tagged as hold-up types compressed into midfield due to the field's numerical imbalance, the race is unlikely to be run at a truly searching tempo — on soft ground over 1m3½f that suits those who can travel close to the pace without expending energy fighting for position. The field holds more true hold-up types than can occupy their natural rear-group positions: Yokohama, Tortured Soul, Green Falcon and Ziggy's Avenger among others are genuine hold-up horses redistributed into midfield on the map because the rear is oversubscribed, meaning genuine closer profiles may find it harder to execute late runs from far back. This race shape most clearly favours horses who can travel prominently or in the first half of the field and sustain their effort through the soft ground, rather than those dependent on a truly fast pace to close into.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Steady Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Star Time sets a sustainable tempo unchallenged and the soft ground blunts the closers' finishing kicks.
scenarios.body: Star Time dictates from the front with Naturalia tracking, and the moderate gallop on testing ground rewards those holding a position in the first half of the field throughout; no strong late surge materialises from the rear because the pace was never fast enough to soften legs ahead of them.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Soft Ground Stayer Grinds
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just fast enough to stretch the field and the soft ground becomes attrition-based, favouring proven soft-ground stamina types.
scenarios.body: Horses with a demonstrated record on soft ground and the stamina to grind out 1m3½f in testing conditions pull clear of those who struggle with the going; hold-up horses with soft-ground form like Flash Bardot and Hamadhan may get into it if they can get a clear run.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Swamp Field
scenarios.trigger: If Naturalia pushes the early pace harder than expected and the front two burn each other out in the soft ground.
scenarios.body: A genuinely draining tempo sets up those sitting midfield or further back to pick off the leaders in the final two furlongs; horses like Yokohama and Lightning Tiger, who are effective on soft ground and capable of a sustained late effort, benefit most.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Star Time settles beautifully, the pace is a complete crawl, and no rival is able to mount a sustained challenge from off the pace.
scenarios.body: With 13 runners on soft ground and a traffic-heavy midfield, a horse who dictates the fractions entirely at their own rhythm and quickens from the front at the two-furlong pole is hardest to peg back; this scenario is unlikely given the number of prominent types who will want to chase Star Time.

watchPoints.text: Star Time is the sole front-runner — watch whether Naturalia immediately contests the lead or settles just behind, as that interaction in the first two furlongs will determine whether this becomes a true soft-ground slog or a tactical crawl.

Flash Bardot has not run for 113 days and returns for Henrietta Knight, who has had only 0 winners from 4 runners in the past 14 days — monitor her at the start and through the early stages for any signs of a ring-rusty performance.

The midfield is severely congested with genuine hold-up horses redistributed forward — watch for a traffic bottleneck on the home turn as Yokohama, Green Falcon, Tortured Soul and Ziggy's Avenger all attempt to find clear daylight from roughly the same position.

Naturalia has placed five times on similar going and represents the most active prominent type behind Star Time — if she travels sweetly into the straight she may prove very hard to stop given the pace map favours hold-a-position runners today.

Lightning Tiger's four consecutive fourth-place finishes suggest a consistent but limited type — watch whether the tongue-tie and today's softer conditions unlock any improvement or simply produce another near-miss.
